Every resource address parsed from infrastructure/ecs/environments/staging and its child modules appears exactly once below. STATUS as of 2026-08-04 (see state-adoption-plan.md §9.9-§9.12): Phase A2 is COMPLETE — all 10 import_unchanged addresses (3 security groups, ALB, 2 listeners, 4 security-group rules) have been imported into the live backend (environments/staging/ecs/terraform.tfstate). State currently contains 10 managed resources plus 9 read-only data-source cache entries. No Phase A3 (import_then_migrate, 16 addresses) resource has been imported. This correction (Phase A3 adoption alignment) reviewed and re-verified, read-only, all 12 addresses not already covered by the four now-imported security-group rules, landed several code fixes (ECS launch-mode/desired-count modeling, cluster capacity-provider representability, IAM inline-policy name alignment), corrected stale prior-audit claims (capacity-provider association, assign_public_ip "hard stop" framing), and recorded a still-open elasticache:ListTagsForResource permission gap. See each entry's notes field for its Group A/B/C readiness classification. No Terraform apply is authorized by any of this — nothing here approves an actual import, ECS deployment, scaling change, capacity-provider association, IAM permission migration, or description-drift reconciliation.

counting_methodology.explanation: Terraform's resource count is variable-dependent (count/for_each conditionals). This manifest counts the resource graph that results when every REQUIRED (no-default) variable is set to the value needed to describe this specific live environment, and every OPTIONAL (has-a-default) variable is left at its current repository default. This is the only way to produce a single deterministic total; a different tfvars file could produce a different count.
required_vars_assumed_set_to_live_values: vpc_id, public_subnet_ids, private_subnet_ids (live default VPC and its subnets)
rds_security_group_id (sg-0d4c5eedb2ee21743, enables the 2 count-gated postgres SG rules)
redis_auth_token (required, no default, sourced from Secrets Manager - enables the replication group)
ses_events_queue_arn, ses_events_queue_url, ses_events_dlq_arn (enables ses_consumer's SQS IAM policy and the 3 SQS-based alarm resources)
ses_sending_identity_arn, ses_authorized_from_address (enables the web task role's SES-send policy)
alarm_sns_topic_arn (has no default; required for the cloudwatch_alarms module to be usable at all)
optional_vars_left_at_repository_default: enable_custom_metric_alarms = false (repository default; app-level custom-metric emission does not exist yet) - excludes 4 alarm resource addresses (queue_depth_high, oldest_queued_job_age_high, failed_jobs_high, scheduler_heartbeat_missing) from the total entirely, since their count expression evaluates to 0

Importing the cluster records the current disabled setting; it does NOT authorize enabling Container Insights later — that requires a separate, explicit cost and observability review. The resource address (module.ecs_cluster.aws_ecs_cluster.this) is unchanged. No exact, source-backed blocker remains — this address is now genuinely suitable for an individual Phase A3 canary import. resources.prerequisite: CORRECTED 2026-08-04: this module previously hardcoded the inline policy's name to "<name_prefix>-task-execution", but the live policy is actually named "FirmsBaseStagingSecretsAccess" (confirmed via aws iam get-role-policy). aws_iam_role_policy's name is effectively immutable (renaming requires delete+recreate) — importing under the live name against the old hardcoded config would have set up a guaranteed REPLACEMENT on the very next plan, not merely a content diff. Fixed: the module now exposes var.task_execution_policy_name (no default, every caller must set it explicitly — mirrors task_execution_role_name's own no-default pattern); this environment's terraform.tfvars sets it to "FirmsBaseStagingSecretsAccess". This aligns identity only. Policy CONTENT still differs materially: live grants exactly secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on 4 named secret ARNs via this inline policy (permissions beyond that come from the separately-attached AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy managed policy); this module's config declares one broader custom inline policy (ECR pull + logs + secrets + KMS) with no managed-policy attachment. That content/permission-shape migration remains the same separate, explicit human decision referenced on the role entry above — not decided or applied here.

resources.prerequisite: Hard stop before any apply (not just import): live service runs assignPublicIp=ENABLED with no NAT gateway anywhere in this VPC (confirmed - default VPC, all-public subnets, sole route table has only an IGW route). Terraform's ecs_service module hardcodes assign_public_ip=false. Applying that in place would cut off all internet egress (ECR/Secrets Manager/CloudWatch Logs/SES/SQS) for every task in the service. Must not apply until the module is fixed to assign_public_ip=true (matching live) or the environment gains real private subnets + NAT. Also: live uses launchType=FARGATE with no capacityProviderStrategy; Terraform uses capacity_provider_strategy exclusively - confirmed non-destructive in-place field swap, safe to accept. Task definition stays pinned per the do_not_import decision above (lifecycle.ignore_changes=[task_definition] already present in the module).
resources.notes: CORRECTED 2026-08-04 (second pass): launch mode and desired count are NO LONGER blockers for this address — both are resolved. Live re-verification (aws ecs describe-services) confirms launchType=FARGATE, capacityProviderStrategy=null, assignPublicIp=ENABLED, desiredCount=1, all now modeled exactly via use_capacity_provider_strategy=false and this role's *_desired_count variable (terraform.tfvars sets it to 1). This address remains Group C (architecture/content migration remains unresolved) in the corrected Phase A3 readiness matrix — see docs/ecs/state-adoption-plan.md §9.12 — for two different, still-open reasons: (1) this module's task_definition argument points at aws_ecs_task_definition.this.arn (a Terraform-managed task definition this module would create fresh), not merely the currently-running historical revision — lifecycle.ignore_changes=[task_definition] prevents an import-time service update from switching to it, but the surrounding configuration's intent (Terraform owns future task-definition revisions) is a real architecture change, not yet reviewed; (2) live services run under a single, generic shared task role, while this module's iam component declares 7 distinct per-role task roles that do not exist live at all. Importing this service does not itself create a task definition or role, but must not be treated as approval to deploy any new Terraform-managed task definition or role-specific task role — that migration is a separate, explicitly reviewed decision.
